text:
PIT outplayed VGK for most of this game and still lost 6-2, with the gap coming down to goaltending and finishing. By expected goals PIT led 2.61 to 2.26, and the simulated replays gave PIT a 57 percent chance of winning. The even-strength gap was wider, 2.54 to 1.76. Sergei Murashov faced 19 shots, allowed five goals, and let in 2.8 more than the chances against him called for. Adin Hill stopped 22 of 24 and saved 0.61 goals above expected.

VGK did their damage early. Rasmus Andersson scored at 1:06 of the first period and Noah Hanifin at 4:02, both snap shots set up by Jack Eichel and Mark Stone. Stone added a power-play goal at 17:46 for a 3-0 lead. In the first period VGK had the better of the chances, 1.12 to 0.90, so the lead was partly earned. Sidney Crosby cut it to 3-1 on a power-play tip-in at 5:54 of the second, but Trevor Connelly answered 71 seconds later on a shot with a 6 percent chance of scoring. Shea Theodore's slap shot at 11:17 made it 5-1.

PIT took over the third, out-chancing VGK 1.05 to 0.54. Evgeni Malkin got one back at 4:43, and Ville Koivunen missed the net on a 31 percent look that was the best chance of the night. Brett Howden then scored at 17:47 on a 5 percent chance, the least likely goal of the game. VGK also won the hits 27 to 10 and the faceoffs 24 to 19 of 43.
